page: Amazon Web Services m5zn.large is a general-purpose, high-clock-speed instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. The hardware is configured with an Intel Xeon Platinum 8252C processor running at a base or sustained frequency of up to 4.5 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. It provides 2 vCPUs distributed across 1 physical core with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system includes 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, offering 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, along with 24 MB of L3 cache. There are no local instance storage disks or dedicated GPUs included in this configuration, requiring attached EBS volumes for persistent storage. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results show a noticeable contrast between single-threaded capabilities and total throughput. Driven by the 4.5 GHz core, single-threaded operations perform moderately well, reflected in an average stress-ng single-core score of 1861.79, a Geekbench single-core score of 1510.0, and a strong single-threaded gzip compression result of 31.71 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics and aggregate compute capacity place in the lower tier due to the limited footprint of 2 vCPUs. Multi-core Geekbench reached 1805.0, while PassMark CPU and memory benchmarks landed in the bottom percentiles.

The primary operational tradeoff centers on per-core clock speed versus overall resource density. Because allocation is limited to 1 physical core and 8 GB of RAM, high-concurrency tasks, extensive parallel compilation, and large-scale data processing face strict bottlenecks. Redis throughput measured at 2.36 million SET operations per second, and LLM text generation via a small 135M parameter model achieved 42.81 tokens per second.

The m5zn.large is suitable for smaller workloads that require elevated clock frequencies rather than parallel thread scalability. Relevant deployments include low-concurrency web serving, gaming servers, lightweight build jobs sensitive to single-thread latency, and basic background utility tasks.
